classification.difficultyReason: Convert megalitres to cubic metres and reverse the cylinder formula for height with final rounding.

content.prompt:
A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 9 metres and a capacity of 1.26 megalitres.

What is the height of the water tank? Give your answer in metres, correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Broad upright cylinder with complete solid top rim, solid vertical silhouettes, solid front bottom arc, dashed rear bottom arc, dotted top radius and external dotted height arrow.
spec.mathematics: Circular ends share a vertical axis. In the projected circular parametrisation x=R cos(t), y=z+e sin(t), sin(t)>0 is the rear half. The viewing direction is from above and the front, making the entire upper rim visible and the rear lower rim hidden. R=9 m is given; projected ellipse aspect and height are illustrative. End discs and curved lateral face determine visibility; radius and height dimensions are separate construction lines.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given radius 9 m and unknown height h.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}V&=1.26\times1000\text{ kL}\\V&=1260\text{ m}^3\\V&=\pi r^2h\\1260&=\pi\times9^2\times h\\1260&=81\pi h\\h&=\frac{1260}{81\pi}\text{ m}\\h&\approx4.95\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
